study type: Quasi-experimental (comparative interrupted time series analysis) with retrospective claims data
exposure: Minnesota's blended payment policy (single payment rate for uncomplicated vaginal and cesarean births)
cohort: The study participants were Medicaid fee-for-service beneficiaries who gave birth in Minnesota and six control states (Wisconsin, Iowa, Illinois, Oregon, Idaho, Montana) between 2006 and 2012.
finding: Following policy implementation, cesarean use decreased more among black women than white women in Minnesota compared to control states, but postpartum hemorrhage increased more significantly among black women.
mod_finding: Policy-related declines in cesarean use were observed among both black and white women in Minnesota, with a larger decline among black women.
